value.name: records codicil suspicions
value.description: Asha notes witness testimony about a codicil executed in October, possible drafting attorney identities, the folder's location, and uncertainties about who accessed the desk.
evidence: *Witness recalls codicil executed October. Drafting attorney possibly Stein/Stine — not Halloran. Folder reportedly placed in bottom right drawer of sewing-room desk. Desk has not yet been opened in my presence. Key in lock. Daniel was in house Saturday between funeral and meeting; access unverified but plausible. Daniel insists no later instrument exists. Lucia knows something she has not said. Rosa terminated by Daniel within 24 hours of funeral.*
value.time_hint: October; Saturday; within 24 hours of funeral

value.name: adds beneficiary question
value.description: Asha appends a note framing the central question of who benefits if the codicil appears or disappears.
evidence: *Question for tomorrow: who benefits from the codicil if it surfaces, and who benefits from it not surfacing, and are those two answers the same.*

value.name: closes investigation notes
value.description: Asha finishes writing, closes the pad, and turns off the kitchen light after reflecting on the house and its occupants.
evidence: She put the pen down. She closed the pad.
Asha turned off the kitchen light.

value.name: lies awake after writing
value.description: Asha does not sleep well that night, having already expected to be unable to rest.
evidence: She did not sleep well. She had not expected to.

value.name: arrives with paralegal at house
value.description: At 9:45 the next morning, Asha stands on the sidewalk in front of the house with her paralegal Marcus, who brings equipment for the visit.
evidence: At nine forty-five the next morning she was on the sidewalk in front of the house with her paralegal, a quiet young man named Marcus who carried a banker's box and a digital camera and asked no questions he had not been asked to ask.
value.location_hint: sidewalk in front of the house
